chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Khālid, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man whose sleep overcomes him, or whom some matter prevents, from praying al-fajr: from the time dawn rises until the sun rises; and that is specifically regarding the obligatory prayer. So if he has prayed one rakʿah of the morning prayer and then the sun rises, then let him complete the salat, and his salat is valid. But if the sun rises before he has prayed one rakʿah, then let him break off the salat and not pray until the sun has risen and its rays have gone away.

key_terms.شُعَاعُهَا: its rays, referring to the sun’s rays

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if sunrise occurs while performing the obligatory fajr prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the obligatory fajr prayer when a person is delayed by sleep or another hindrance. If one rakʿah has been completed before sunrise, the prayer is completed and counts as valid; if sunrise occurs before one rakʿah, the prayer is to be stopped and delayed until after the sun has risen and its rays have diminished.
